response.passage: To understand triangles, we must look at their unique properties. First, consider the angle sum property: the sum of all three interior angles in any triangle is always exactly 180 degrees, regardless of the triangle's size or shape. A common mistake is thinking larger triangles have larger angle sums, but this is false. Second, let us look at the sides. For any three lengths to form a triangle, the sum of the lengths of any two sides must be strictly greater than the length of the third side. If the sum equals the third side, the lines will simply lie flat and never meet to form a triangle. Third, consider the altitude. An altitude is a line segment drawn from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side. Unlike a median, which always bisects the opposite side, an altitude does not have to bisect the side it meets. Finally, let us apply the Pythagoras property, which is exclusive to right-angled triangles. If a triangle has sides a, b, and hypotenuse c, then a squared plus b squared must equal c squared. After calculating the sum of the squares, you must find the square root to determine the final length of the hypotenuse.
response.summary: Triangles follow strict rules regarding their angles, side lengths, and altitudes. The angle sum is always 180 degrees, and side lengths must satisfy the triangle inequality. Right-angled triangles specifically follow the Pythagoras property.
